ALG-H5-01.solved: Infinitely many solutions means the second equation is a multiple of the first. -15y = 3(-5y), so the factor is 3: a = 9, b = 3(12) = 36. a + b = 45.
ALG-H5-01.note: 36 catches a student who reports b alone; 21 = 9 + 12. One idea (proportionality of coefficients) applied once.

ALG-H5-02.note: 16 is the boundary (costs are equal there, 432 = 432) and is the one real trap; 7 and 9 correspond to no path I can construct.

ALG-H5-03.note: Pure two-point-slope computation, no second idea.

ALG-H5-04.solved: Need 2x - 8 >= 0, so x >= 4. Case x - 10 = 2x - 8 gives x = -2, rejected. Case 10 - x = 2x - 8 gives 3x = 18, x = 6. Check: |6-10| = 4 = 2(6)-8.
ALG-H5-04.note: -2 is the genuine extraneous root, the best distractor in the batch. Still a standard SAT medium: absolute-value casework with a validity check is the single routine taught for this item type.

ALG-H5-05.note: Textbook mixture setup. 40 (the other solution's volume) is notably absent from the options, which is the distractor a real mixture item would carry.

ALG-H5-06.solved: 5x - 8 > 17 -> x > 5. 2x + 1 < 41 -> x < 20. x integer, so greatest is 19.
ALG-H5-06.note: 20 is the non-strict-inequality slip, 6 the least value. Two inequalities but they do not interact - each is solved independently and only one bound is read.

ALG-H5-07.note: 8 is the floor/boundary trap. Same crossover structure as ALG-H5-02; the two are near-duplicates in method.

ALG-H5-08.note: Substitute and solve, three lines. 39 catches failing to divide by 3. This is an easy item by any module's standard.

ALG-H5-09.note: 51 (forgetting the -8) is a strong distractor, but recognizing the multiple is a single standard move.

ALG-H5-10.solved: 4x + 10y = 15 -> slope -2/5; perpendicular slope 5/2. Through (10, -1): y = -1 + (5/2)(x - 10); at x = 0, y = -1 - 25 = -26.
ALG-H5-10.note: 24 is the sign slip on the intercept. Two steps (perpendicular slope, then intercept) but they chain rather than interact.

ALG-H5-11.solved: First 8 minutes: 96 pages. Remaining 396 - 96 = 300 pages at 20/min = 15 min. Total 8 + 15 = 23.
ALG-H5-11.note: 15 (reporting only the second phase) and 33 (= 396/12) are both real wrong paths.

ALG-H5-12.solved: 15x - 10 + a = bx + 6. No solution requires equal x-coefficients and unequal constants: b = 15 (with a != 16).
ALG-H5-12.note: 16 is the value of a that would instead give infinitely many solutions - a good distractor. The item asks only for b, so the a-condition never has to be stated; that is what keeps it from being hard.

ALG-H5-13.note: 160 (stopping at the original) and 142 (= 102 + 40, applying the offset to the reduced price) are both natural. Multi-step but each step is routine percent work.

ALG-H5-14.solved: s + l = 54 and 3s = l + 14. Substituting l = 54 - s: 3s = 68 - s -> s = 17, l = 37.
ALG-H5-14.note: Standard two-equation word problem; 'exceeds by' is the only wrinkle.

ALG-H5-15.solved: 180 + 45d <= 2300 -> 45d <= 2120 -> d <= 47.1, so at most 47 days. But d must be a multiple of 7: 42 (cost 2070). 49 days would cost 2385 > 2300.
ALG-H5-15.note: The one item in the batch where two constraints genuinely interact: the budget bound and the whole-weeks divisibility must be combined, and the answer is not the floor of the budget bound. 47 is exactly the one-idea answer and 49 the round-up-to-the-next-week answer; both are strong. Low-end hard, but hard.

ALG-H5-16.note: 5 is the original x-intercept, 3 the translate-down slip. One-step transformation.

ALG-H5-17.note: Same system-substitution shape as ALG-H5-05 and ALG-H5-14; the batch reuses this template three times.

ALG-H5-18.note: 26 (rounding up; 502 > 500) is the real trap. The integer constraint is only a floor, so the two conditions chain rather than interact - this is the medium version of what ALG-H5-15 does properly.

ALG-H5-19.note: 11 is the answer if you solve for the input a - 2 and stop; 39 skips the division. Strong options, easy item.

ALG-H5-20.solved: Let pears = 4k, apples = 7k. 4k/(7k + 12) = 4/9 -> 36k = 28k + 48 -> k = 6. Apples before = 42.
ALG-H5-20.note: 24 = pears, 54 = apples after, 6 = k. Every distractor is a quantity the student actually computes - the best-built option set in the batch.

ALG-H5-21.note: Requires taking the extremes in opposite directions, which is the closest any other item comes to two interacting ideas. 30 (the centers' difference) and 4 (the minimum) are reasonable. Still a single standard interval-arithmetic move; upper medium.

ALG-H5-22.note: 19 = 95/5 (ignoring the +10 offset) is the only live wrong path.

ALG-H5-23.note: 7 (answering with x instead of f(x)) is the whole point of the item and a strong distractor. The algebra itself is easy.

ALG-H5-24.note: Fourth 'greatest value under an inequality' item in the batch (with 06, 15, 18). This one is the bare one-line version.
